# Methane trapped in Antarctic ice cores

Antarctic ice cores preserve ancient air in bubbles that close off at the bottom
of the firn column. The methane concentration of that air is the direct record of
the atmospheric burden at the time of closure, without any proxy inversion.

## Air bubbles and firn densification

Firn turns into ice between fifty and a hundred metres of depth, and the bubbles
seal over a span of decades rather than an instant. That gas age distribution is
the uncertainty budget of every ice core methane series: the ice matrix dates the
snowfall, the bubble dates the air.

Methane rises sharply at each deglaciation, in step with the temperature
reconstruction from the same core, and the lag between the two is still argued
over in the literature.
